bugs: ApplyDiscountRequest.php:45 runs strtoupper(trim()) on the input but compares it to the stored code exactly. Any code stored in lower or mixed case (e.g. 'summer10') can never be redeemed and gets 'does not exist' (confirmed with a probe).

DiscountCode.php:53 checks for 'no eligible lines' even when the code has no category restriction. On an empty cart, an unrestricted code (even free_shipping) gets a 422 with the broken message 'only applies to items in the  category.' (confirmed with a probe).
DiscountCode.php:53 also rejects a category-restricted free_shipping code when no line matches, even though line eligibility has nothing to do with free shipping.

app/Pricing/PriceCart.php:57-65 has two sequential `if` blocks on the enum type where a `match` would be clearer
app/Pricing/PriceCart.php:64 merges with `$shares + $discounts`, an array-union trick that is easy to misread
app/Models/DiscountCode.php:21-24 and CartItem.php:17-23 add redundant integer casts on integer columns
app/Http/Requests/ApplyDiscountRequest.php:45 reads raw input() instead of validated()

strengths: Single-action controller that calls a pricing action with method injection
Validation lives in FormRequest after() hooks with a separate message for each failure reason, and the validity logic sits on the model (rejectionReason)
Fixed-amount spread caps each line's extra at its line total, so lines always sum exactly
Uses the #[Fillable] attribute, a casts() method, a backed enum and factory states

bugs: Minor: percentage discounts are rounded per line, so cart-level rounding can drift (3×105 at 10% gives 33, not 32). Defensible, but worth noting.
Minor: a category-restricted code with no matching lines is accepted with a discount of 0 instead of a clear 422. Not strictly required by the task.
antipatterns: app/Pricing/CalculateCartPricing.php:20 types DiscountCode as nullable and does null-handling, even though the FormRequest guarantees a code (speculative generality)
app/Http/Requests/ApplyDiscountRequest.php:54 calls load('items') and the controller then calls loadMissing (ApplyDiscountController.php:15), so loading happens in two places
tests/Feature/ApplyDiscountTest.php:21 calls Http::preventStrayRequests with no HTTP usage (ceremony)
routes/api.php:7 adds a throttle middleware nobody asked for (harmless)
strengths: Thinnest controller of the three: one line, an injected invokable action, and a response wrapped in 'data'
FormRequest after() hook uses match(true) for an ordered, single error per failure reason, and once() memoizes the code lookup through validated()
Pricing uses collections throughout (filter/sum/mapWithKeys/map), with a match on the backed enum
Proportional fixed-amount allocation, with leftover cents distributed and a cap at the eligible total
Most thorough test suite: boundary tests at the min subtotal, the free-shipping threshold and max uses, an empty cart, min subtotal checked against the whole cart, and no use consumed

bugs: Minor: the min-subtotal error hardcodes the currency (Number::currency(..., in: 'DKK')), an assumption the task never states, and it depends on the intl extension
Minor: percentage discounts are rounded per line (3×105 at 10% gives 33), the same as impl-2
Minor: the column is named unit_price, which loses the 'cents' unit the spec emphasises
antipatterns: app/Pricing/BuildCartPriceBreakdown.php:65-66 drops from collections to ->all() arrays and then runs imperative foreach loops that mutate a passed-in $discounts array (pass-around state)
app/Pricing/BuildCartPriceBreakdown.php:76-113 has percentage/fixed helpers that take and return the accumulator array, which is more ceremony than a map
app/Http/Requests/ApplyDiscountRequest.php:41 relies on an @var annotation where a typed helper would do, and items are lazy-loaded rather than loaded explicitly
strengths: One-line invokable controller with an injected pricing action
FormRequest after() with match(true) returns a single, ordered error per reason, with a test proving only the first failure is reported
Zero-initialises every line's discount and guards eligibleTotal === 0, so it is robust for empty carts and categories with no matches
Fixed allocation guards each increment so no line goes below zero
Good tests: threshold boundaries, a future expiry, remaining uses, a category not in the cart, rounding, and no use consumed

v.rationale: I ran the suites, read every added file, and probed each implementation with throwaway tests (since deleted). All three suites pass (impl-2: 24 tests, impl-3: 23, impl-1: 20), and all three share the same architecture: an invokable controller, a FormRequest whose after() hook gives one error per failure reason, and a pricing action on Laravel 13.40. impl-2 ranks first. It uses collections most consistently, has the cleanest one-line controller, and its tests cover the most edge cases. Its only issues are cosmetic: a nullable code parameter in the pricing action and items loaded in two places. impl-3 is close behind but scores a little lower on idiom. It drops into arrays with mutable accumulators, hardcodes the DKK currency in an error message, and its unit_price column name loses the cents unit. impl-1 ranks last because of real bugs I confirmed with probes. It uppercases the input before an exact-match lookup, so lowercase stored codes can never be redeemed. It also applies a 'no eligible lines' check to unrestricted codes, so an empty cart gets a 422 with the broken message 'only applies to items in the  category.', and a free-shipping code is rejected the same way. Its pricing code also relies on raw array_* functions instead of collections.
